rules.title: Prohibition on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy levels (BMC Chapter 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide a coordinated pricing algorithm to Berkeley landlords, and unlawful for a landlord to use one to set rents or occupancy levels for residential units in Berkeley; each unit and each month of a violation is a separate violation. The City Attorney may sue over sale or use of such an algorithm, and aggrieved tenants may sue over a landlord's use, for injunctive relief, damages and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on selling or using coordinated pricing algorithms; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; Competitor Data = non-public data less than 90 days old
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Applies to landlords and to anyone who sells or licenses such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions: The following are excluded from the definition of coordinated pricing algorithm: (a) products or processes that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, occupancy rates or terms; (b) products used to set rent or income limits under local, state or federal affordable housing guidelines; (c) products or processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord.
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.63; Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley

levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance: Annual General Adjustment limit on rent increases (as amended by Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully covered units may raise rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), which the Rent Board sets at 65% of the Bay Area CPI increase and which Measure BB caps at 5%. Banked (unused) AGAs may still raise rent above 5% up to the rent ceiling, and Regulation 1148 sets the eligibility and tenant-notice conditions for taking the increase.
rules.key_value: AGA = 65% of Bay Area CPI-U increase, capped at 5%; 2026 AGA is 1.0% (65% of a 1.5% CPI increase), effective no earlier than 2026-01-01
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered (rent ceiling and AGA limit apply): most units in multifamily properties built before 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996; rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented individually under separate leases). Government-subsidized units (e.g., Housing Choice Voucher/Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME) fall within these categories where Federal or State law does not prohibit rent control. Utility charges for fully covered units must be included in base rent unless the utility is separately metered and the lease requires the tenant to hold the account.
rules.exemptions: Not subject to rent control (partially covered, registration only): new construction with a Certificate of Occupancy issued after June 1980; single-family homes with tenancies that began on or after January 1, 1996; most condominiums. Exempt: 'Golden Duplex' units (owner-occupied on Dec. 31, 1979, with an owner currently living in one unit); units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the owner, if the owner lived on the property at the start of the tenancy. Section 202, Section 811, and HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgage projects with Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside or Project-based Section 8 subsidies are not rent-controlled. The 2026 AGA does not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.interaction: Government-subsidized units are fully covered by the rent ceiling only where Federal law, State law, or administrative regulation does not prohibit rent control.

rules.requirement: Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, including refusing to rent, evicting, charging more, or refusing to add a family member based on criminal history. rules.title: Cartwright Act: ban on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute one while coercing another person to set or adopt its recommended price or commercial term for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.key_value: Unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (any methodology, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or influence a price or commercial term) (a) as part of a restraint-of-trade conspiracy, or (b) while coercing others to adopt its recommended price or commercial term
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person, other than the end consumer, who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm for products or services in California. The law covers all industries and is not limited to rental housing, so it reaches residential rent-setting.
rules.exemptions: Only algorithms used by two or more persons that use competitor data are covered. Single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data fall outside the definition. A secondary source notes that the statute does not expressly exempt non-confidential competitor data.
rules.interaction: Nothing in the section impairs or limits the applicability of antitrust laws.
rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (added by Stats. 2025, ch. 338 (AB 325)); see also Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16756.1
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.penalty: Cartwright Act violations are punishable as a crime, per the Legislative Counsel's Digest; no specific penalty is stated in the bill text.
rules.subject: landlord
supporting_spans: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act: just cause required to terminate tenancies
rules.requirement: Once a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may terminate the tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written termination notice. If adult tenants were added before any existing tenant reached 24 months, this applies only once all tenants have 12 months or any tenant has 24 months. For no-fault terminations, the owner must either pay relocation assistance equal to one month's rent within 15 calendar days of serving the notice or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of occupancy (if adult tenants were added, once all tenants have 12 months or any tenant has 24 months); no-fault relocation assistance of one month's rent, paid within 15 calendar days of service of the notice, or waiver of the final month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property whose tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied it for the required period. The section does not apply to property covered by a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended later if that ordinance is more protective. A property is not subject to both.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, extended care facilities, licensed residential care facilities for the elderly, and adult residential facilities; school or university dormitories; tenants who share a bathroom or kitchen with an owner-occupant; owner-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes where the owner lived in one unit at the start of the tenancy; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property such as single-family homes or condominiums owned by natural persons, subject to the statute's conditions.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended after that date that is more protective than this section (the local ordinance applies instead). A property is not subject to both. A later local ordinance that is less protective is not enforced unless this section is repealed. Yields to local rules: BERK-EVICT-01, BERK-EVICT-02, LA-EVICT-01, LA-EVICT-02, LA-EVICT-03, SD-EVICT-01, SF-EVICT-01, SA-EVICT-01.

rules.penalty: A notice is void if the owner does not strictly comply. rules.title: California statewide rent cap (Tenant Protection Act of 2019, AB 1482, as amended by SB 567)
rules.requirement: Over any 12-month period, an owner of covered residential real property may not raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. The increase is measured against the lowest gross rental rate charged in the prior 12 months, and no more than two increases are allowed in 12 months for the same tenant. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession.

rules.exemptions: (1) Deed-restricted or government-agreement affordable housing for very low, low or moderate income households, or housing subject to an affordability subsidy agreement. (4) Housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless it is a mobilehome. (5) Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, such as single-family homes and condominiums. rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not pay for or subscribe to a coordinator's services, and no person may perform a coordinating function or engage in or facilitate parallel pricing coordination using algorithms that rely on competitors' competitively sensitive information to set or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy levels. Violations are unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act, and the Attorney General must establish a complaint location and may adopt rules.
rules.key_value: Ban on use of algorithmic revenue management software or algorithmic devices performing a coordinating function (shared nonpublic data / parallel pricing coordination) for residential rents; effective July 1, 2027
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential dwelling units in New Jersey (houses, apartments, accessory units or other units intended as a primary residence) and to any rental property owner, coordinator or other person. Municipalities may not enact conflicting ordinances, except ordinances explicitly authorized or required by any other law.
rules.exemptions: Residential dwelling units exclude inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. Government entities are not 'coordinators', and parallel pricing required by affordability controls is not covered. Algorithmic devices exclude spreadsheets that do not use AI and require human analysis.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of the just causes listed in Section 37.9(a), and that cause must be the dominant motive; expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause. Evictions for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of a unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation also require relocation payments under Section 37.9C.
rules.key_value: 17 just cause reasons under Section 37.9(a)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. Some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits remain subject to the just cause eviction provisions. These include units whose first Certificate of Occupancy was issued after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, and some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.exemptions: Relocation payments for temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 rather than Rent Ordinance § 37.9C.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
rules.penalty: Substantial civil and/or criminal liability for unlawful eviction or attempted eviction.

supporting_spans: Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance: annual allowable rent increase limits
rules.requirement: For units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits, the annual allowable increase from March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent (base rent × .016). The prior periods were 1.4% (3/1/2025–2/28/2026) and 1.7% (3/1/2024–2/28/2025).
